newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures end weaker on bullion freefall.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures end weaker on bullion freefall.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo gold futures ended weaker on Thursday, pushed down by a continuing freefall in spot gold prices and the yen's fall against the dollar later in the day, traders said.
Gold prices ranged from flat to four yen per gram lower, with the most-active benchmark December ending down three at 1,310 yen.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $384.50/80 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $355.70/356.10 in New York on Wednesday.
"During Asian hours, we were seeing significant selling by overseas investors in the spot market. The next target will be at $350.00 per ounce," one trader said.
In the gold futures market, constant bargain-hunting buying tended to be overwhelmed by selling pressure amid bearish sentiment.

A plunge in the Japanese stock market on Thursday, with the Nikkei 225 share index falling 606.51 points to end at 18,073.87, had no immediate impact on the precious metals market, but the gloomy outlook for Japan's economy could undermine platinum futures in the longer term.
Platinum futures were mostly lower in tandem with gold. Silver was mixed.
The only bright spot was in palladium futures, which ranged from four to eight yen per gram higher. Benchmark December palladium was up five yen at 447 yen.
"Physical demand supported palladium prices. Constant profit-taking by individual investors on TOCOM was absorbed by physical buying," one trader said.
Benchmark December silver was up 1.2 yen per 10 grams firmer at 176.9 yen. Benchmark December platinum was flat at 1,332 yen. -- Tokyo Commodity Desk +81-3-3432-7431
